Acceptance for registration may then be allowed on the basis of a limitation to colour."},{"ref":"TMM/Part10/3/3/5/3~1","quote":"If an applicant chooses to limit to colour during examination, this same form of endorsement would be the appropriate one."},{"ref":"TMM/Part22/25/25/8","quote":"As such a trade mark which consists entirely of a simple barcode is unlikely to be prima facie capable of distinguishing."},{"ref":"TMM/Part22/25/25/8","quote":"In contrast a trade mark which contains a barcode along with other material would need to be considered as a whole, in a similar manner to other composite trade marks."},{"ref":"TMM/Part21/4/4/1~2","quote":"“The trade mark is limited to the colours green and blue as shown in the representation attached to the application form.”"},{"ref":"TMM/Part21/4/4/1~2","quote":"Descriptions for COLOURED trade marks which are allowable but will not be considered to be indicative of a restriction or limitation to colour"},{"ref":"TMM/Part21/4/4/1~2","quote":"“The trade mark is depicted in the colours green and blue as shown in the representation attached to the application form.”"}],"answer":"The supplied passages do not establish that always using a barcode in green and blue automatically requires a colour limitation. I cannot determine whether your particular application would need one.

Under **Manual practice—not legislation**, a colour limitation may be relevant where a mark lacks inherent adaptation to distinguish, but evidence of use shows that it distinguishes when used in particular colours. An applicant may also choose to limit to colour during examination [TMM/Part10/3/3/5/3~1].

The barcode must still be considered for distinctiveness: the Manual says a mark consisting entirely of a simple barcode is unlikely to be prima facie capable of distinguishing; a barcode with other material must be considered as a whole [TMM/Part22/25/25/8].

If a colour limitation is intended, the Manual recognises wording such as: “The trade mark is limited to the colours green and blue as shown in the representation attached to the application form.” Merely saying that the mark is “depicted” in those colours is not treated as a colour restriction [TMM/Part21/4/4/1~2].

No Act or Regulations passages were supplied, so this explanation is confined to Manual practice."}
